answer: In this PoA design, each bonded identity commits collateral, and correlated equivocation across k coordinated identities triggers aggregate penalties proportional to O(k²), making synchronized false votes increasingly costly. A detected sybil swarm also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, including bonded escrows and asymmetric depreciation, so one operator cannot cheaply fragment risk across aliases. The comet, ripple, and pigment markers are irrelevant to penalty attribution unless they encode shared control.
